payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, f(x + 1) = f(x).

dependency_self_check.notes: The proof only uses the definition of f from the allowed semantic anchor and a standard floor identity.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n>1 be fixed, and define f(x)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}. We show that f(x+1)=f(x) for every real x.

For each integer k with 1\le k\le n, since k is an integer we have
\[
\lfloor k(x+1)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+k\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+k,
\]
because adding an integer shifts the floor by the same integer.
Also,
\[
\lfloor n(x+1)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+n\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+n.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x+1)
&=\lfloor n(x+1)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\lfloor k(x+1)\rfloor}{k} \\
&=(\lfloor nx\rfloor+n)-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+k}{k} \\
&=(\lfloor nx\rfloor+n)-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^{n}1 \\
&=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k} \\
&=f(x),
\end{aligned}
\]
since \(\sum_{k=1}^{n}1=n\). Hence f(x+1)=f(x) for all real x.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the floor shift identity \(\lfloor t+m\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+m\) for integers m. Apply it to each term with m=k and m=n, then the added integers cancel in the definition of f.

used_external_facts: For any real t and integer m, \(\lfloor t+m\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+m\).
